identifier: Payment options for hemp sales on Shopify
statement: Shopify Payments doesn't support the sale of hemp, cannabidiol (CBD), and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) products.

identifier: Shopify Payments and third-party payment providers
statement: Currently, Shopify Payments doesn’t support the sale of hemp and hemp derived CBD and THC products. However, Shopify has partnered with integrated third-party payment providers that support the sale of these products.
Approval decisions are at the discretion of each third-party payment provider, and Shopify can’t guarantee the approval of your store.

identifier: Using Shopify after being removed from Shopify Payments
statement: If Shopify Payments was removed from your store due to the sale of hemp products, then you may still be able to use Shopify to host your store when processing payments through an alternative third-party payment provider.

If you’re a US merchant selling hemp products, or a Canadian merchant selling cannabis products, then you must agree to the requirements set by Shopify. These requirements ensure that you understand and will comply with the regulations for selling hemp products on Shopify.
If you’re selling hemp products on Shopify, then SMS notifications aren’t supported for this specific category of products.
However, you can’t use any POS hardware that requires the use of Shopify Payments.
If you use Managed Markets to sell to customers in the European Union, then compliant cancellation and return policies are automatically applied to your Managed Markets orders.
If you sell to consumers in the EU, then you can use Shopify's return and cancellation rules to help meet the electronic withdrawal function requirement.
Managed Markets doesn't support some countries or regions, and currencies.
Your store currency must be the default currency of the country where your business is based.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in the United States
statement: Your business needs to be based in the continental United States (exclusive of territories including Puerto Rico and Guam).

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: If you have fulfillment locations in both Great Britain and Northern Ireland, then you can't use Managed Markets.

statement: Delivered duty unpaid (DDU) shipping remains available only in countries and regions where DDP isn't supported.
Shopify Protect for Managed Markets is available only for stores in the United States.
Managed Markets doesn't support multiple business entities in a single store.

identifier: EU right of withdrawal in Managed Markets
statement: All Managed Markets orders into the EU are subject to the same cancellation and return policies.

This setting is in your admin at **Settings** > [**Customer accounts**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/customer_accounts), and requires you to agree to use your own solution for returns and cancellations for Managed Markets in the European Union.

identifier: Prohibited and restricted items on Managed Markets
statement: If you sell a product that's prohibited in a destination country, then Managed Markets hides the product from the catalog for customers in that country.

identifier: Prohibited and restricted items on Managed Markets
statement: Every country has their own restrictions for what kinds of goods can be shipped into that country. Shipping carriers and payment processors have their own restrictions as well.

statement: With Shopify Markets on its own, you remain the [merchant of record](#merchant-of-record), so tax registration, duties, and customs compliance stay your responsibility. Managed Markets adds Global-e as the merchant of record and takes those responsibilities on for a per-order fee.
Markets that you deactivate will no longer use Managed Markets as a merchant of record. You become responsible for tax compliance and regulatory requirements in those markets.

If your primary market isn't in the EEA, but you use international sales tools (such as Markets or Global‑e) to sell products to customers in the EEA, then compare‑at prices for these customers are displayed by default.
If your primary market is in the EEA, then the compare-at price feature is always displayed.

identifier: Checkout behavior on stores with one-page checkout access
statement: If a customer chooses to ship to a country or region that differs from the one that they selected on your storefront, then a checkout restriction applies that changes their currency to match their shipping destination at checkout.
Checkout restrictions help provide a consistent checkout experience that prevents customers from having to pay additional fees, such as conversion fees, through their credit card companies.
Your setting for Shopify Network Intelligence takes effect globally, but your settings for cookie banners and data sharing can be managed per region.
The region picker cards, which include a dialog listing all available countries and states, are used for configuring where the consent banner and opt-out page are displayed in your online store.

Any event data transmitted to Google from customers, such as those located in the European Economic Area (EEA), won't be used for personalized advertising unless Google Consent Mode v2 is activated and valid consent is obtained.
In the **Customer data hosting location** section, you can find the primary location where Shopify stores your store data, order data, and customer personal data.
The requirement for each additional address field depends on the customer's country or region and can't be changed.

Customer regions with the email marketing consent checkbox preselected are chosen based on the latest recommendations from Shopify. These automatic recommendations don't constitute legal advice, and you're responsible for complying with your local laws and regulations.
If you sell to customers in certain countries and regions, then the checkout displays additional required tax fields.

identifier: Change contact information for .at and .fr domains
statement: Due to Austrian and French regulations, [WHOIS](/manual/domains/domains-terminology#whois-privacy) contact information for `.at` and `.fr` domains cannot be updated from your Shopify admin.
EU domain extensions (such as .DE, .IT, .EU, .BE, .NL) may require identity verification to comply with NIS2 regulations.

As a result of Brexit, Visa and Mastercard have changed how they classify and charge for United Kingdom (UK) and European Union (EU) transactions. To comply with these changes, Shopify classifies these transactions as international, and you're charged at the current international rate for your region.

identifier: Bank account and personal information requirements for Shopify Payments in France
statement: Before using Shopify Payments in France, you need to understand the requirements that are in place to comply with regulations and to prevent financial crimes.
By default, receipts generated through Shopify POS are compliant with the requirements of supported regulated markets.
Receipt appearance and fields can't be changed within Shopify.
Content that's required for Marque NF525 compliance can't be customized or removed.
Depending on where your store is located, there might be local requirements that you need to meet to sell in person.
In France, Spain, Italy, Germany, and Sweden, a return or exchange against an original sale must be processed by the same legal entity as the original sale to be compliant.
There are no exceptions for merchants in France. In other regulated POS markets, merchants can make their own business decision, but cross-entity returns and exchanges aren't fiscalized.

identifier: Eligibility for tax summaries on receipts
statement: Tax summaries and tax registration numbers on printed receipts are available only for stores that calculate tax with Basic Tax or Shopify Tax.

identifier: Eligibility for tax summaries on receipts
statement: If your store uses a third-party tax service, such as Avalara, TaxJar, or Vertex, or the legacy external tax service, then your printed receipts can display tax lines without tax registration numbers.
Shopify POS doesn't include gross turnover (GTO) reporting functionality. However, there are several third-party solutions for sending gross turnover reports.
If your store operates in Spain, then you're required to comply with Fiscalization requirements by January 1, 2026.
With Comply, Shopify POS operates in compliance with current Veri*Factu obligations in Spain by enabling automatic auditing of all Shopify POS transactions in Spain.
You can't sell product bundles in Shopify POS for retail locations in Spain.

identifier: Set up the Comply app for fiscal compliance in Spain
statement: It appears you have one or more retail locations in Spain. To ensure your Shopify POS system is operating optimally in Spain, and avoid potential penalties, you should install the Comply app now.
Marque NF525 certification for Shopify POS is issued through Infocert, a third-party certification service.

Marque NF525 certification for Shopify POS is eligible for stores in France that have Shopify Payments activated. If you use a third-party payment provider, then your payment configuration might not be covered by Shopify's NF525 certification.

identifier: Set up the Comply app for fiscal compliance in France
statement: If you use Shopify POS version 11.3 or later, then you must activate Comply before you can accept in-person sales. If you uninstall Comply, then sales are blocked until Comply is installed and activated again.
To comply with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), POS receipts don't include information about your POS staff.
